mismatch.message: nh_timeout()'s run_timers() requires a ported timeout function, but revive_mon() is due

summary: At segment 0 step 89, a time-advancing wait reaches nh_timeout()'s final run_timers(). C dispatches the due TIMER_OBJECT/REVIVE_MON callback for the wished troll corpse; JS refuses because timeout_funcs[REVIVE_MON] has no handler. The corpse is in hero inventory, so after dispatch is wired, do.c:revive_mon also needs the inventory branch of do.c:revive_corpse; the current JS helper supports only floor corpses.

source.branch: An ordinary, non-Rider troll corpse wished into hero inventory has reached its due REVIVE_MON object timer during an elapsed wait. The C callback should revive the corpse and report it squirming from the backpack; displacer and failed-revival retry branches are not reached by this case.
callers: timeout.c:nh_timeout calls run_timers() at its tail; timeout.c:run_timers dispatches timeout_funcs[REVIVE_MON].f to do.c:revive_mon. js/timeout.js has a revive_mon table row with no handler, so its due-timer preflight stops the turn.

do.c:revive_mon calls do.c:revive_corpse(body). The existing js/do.js helper implements only OBJ_FLOOR and throws for other locations; this recipe wishes the troll corpse into inventory (recorded step 47 says “p - a troll corpse”).

mkobj.c:set_corpsenm calls start_corpse_timeout, which schedules the troll REVIVE_MON timer. The JS timeout setup already reaches the same due callback with matching prior RNG, so retain that timer creation and wire its dispatch.

Existing revive_corpse callers remain through the shared JS helper: hack.c:revive_nasty, pickup.c:rider_corpse_revival, eat.c:eatcorpse, apply.c tinning, teleport.c:rloco, and monster corpse handling in mon.c. Preserve their existing call paths while adding the whole location behavior.
dependencies: Read whole do.c:revive_corpse (2111-2250) and revive_mon (2251-2292). Port all revive_corpse location arms (OBJ_INVENT, OBJ_FLOOR, OBJ_MINVENT, OBJ_CONTAINED, OBJ_BURIED), including source messages and buried-troll handling; do not leave the current non-floor refusal.

Reuse the already ported zap.c:revive() result and corpse removal, plus existing timer start_timer(), obj_has_timer(), mkobj.c:rider_revival_time(), and the ROT_CORPSE callback. Preserve revive_mon failed-revival scheduling and timer ownership; the current recipe covers only a successful troll revival from inventory.
Wire the do.c:revive_mon callback into timeout.c:timeout_funcs[REVIVE_MON] and js/timeout.js. Do not claim the separate ZOMBIFY_MON timer callback or other unported timeout-table rows.
